resumen: Los ~60 irregulares más frecuentes agrupados por sonido: base → pasado → participio, siempre dentro de una frase.

teoria.paraQue: Los verbos irregulares no llevan -ed: cambian de forma. Son pocos (unos 60 cubren casi todo lo que se habla) pero son los más usados: go, have, make, get, say, take, see. Sin ellos no se puede contar nada en pasado.
teoria.llave: Cada verbo tiene tres formas: base → pasado → participio. La base va después de las llaves (did, didn't, will, used to). El pasado va solo en la afirmativa del pasado simple. El participio va después de have/has (presente perfecto) y de be (pasiva). Aprenderlos por familias de sonido es más fácil que en orden alfabético.
reglas: Familia -ought / -aught (suenan igual, /ɔːt/): buy → bought → bought · bring → brought → brought · think → thought → thought · teach → taught → taught · catch → caught → caught · fight → fought → fought.
Familia i → a → u: sing → sang → sung · ring → rang → rung · drink → drank → drunk · begin → began → begun · swim → swam → swum. (Run → ran → run es la excepción.)
Familia -ew → -own: know → knew → known · grow → grew → grown · throw → threw → thrown · blow → blew → blown · fly → flew → flown · draw → drew → drawn.

Familia -o- → -en: write → wrote → written · drive → drove → driven · ride → rode → ridden · speak → spoke → spoken · break → broke → broken · choose → chose → chosen · wake → woke → woken · steal → stole → stolen · freeze → froze → frozen.
Familia -ook / -ake: take → took → taken · shake → shook → shaken · mistake → mistook → mistaken.

Familia terminada en -t (pasado = participio): send → sent · spend → spent · build → built · lend → lent · lose → lost · leave → left · feel → felt · keep → kept · sleep → slept · meet → met · mean → meant · sit → sat · get → got (participio gotten).
Familia -old / -ound / -ood (pasado = participio): tell → told · sell → sold · find → found · stand → stood · understand → understood.
Familia pasado = participio con cambio de vocal: say → said · pay → paid · make → made · have → had · hear → heard · read → read (se escribe igual, suena /red/) · win → won · wear → wore → worn.
Familia tres formas iguales: put · cut · let · cost · hit · hurt · set · shut. Put → put → put.

Los salvajes (cada uno a su manera): go → went → gone · do → did → done · see → saw → seen · eat → ate → eaten · give → gave → given · come → came → come · become → became → become · forget → forgot → forgotten · fall → fell → fallen · be → was/were → been.

teoria.tip: Aprende cada verbo cantado en su familia (bought, brought, thought, taught) y siempre dentro de una frase tuya. Un verbo suelto se olvida; una frase se queda.

ejercicios.explica: Familia i → a: el pasado cambia la i por a (el participio por u: sung, rung, drunk).
Familia -ew: knew, grew, threw, flew, drew. Participios en -own / -awn.
Familia con o en el pasado: wrote, drove, spoke, broke, chose. Participios en -en.
Familia -t: el pasado y el participio son iguales (sent, sent).
Pasado ↔ participio: el participio va después de have/has.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta cinco cosas que hiciste ayer usando solo verbos irregulares (went, had, took, made, saw, ate, bought…).
ejercicios.objetivo: Pasado simple afirmativo con cinco irregulares distintos.
ejercicios.ejemplo: Yesterday I woke up at 6, had breakfast with my family and took the bus to the office. At lunch I ate with Camila, and in the evening I saw a movie.
ejercicios.explica: Di cada verbo en pasado con claridad: woke, had, took, ate, saw. Si dudas, repite la familia en voz alta.

ejercicios.consigna: Describe la última reunión con un cliente usando al menos cinco irregulares: met, told, said, brought, gave, chose, thought.
ejercicios.objetivo: Pasado simple con irregulares de trabajo.
ejercicios.ejemplo: On Tuesday we met the client at her office. We brought the printed deck and told her the plan. She said she liked it, gave us some feedback and chose the second route.
ejercicios.explica: Met, brought, told, said, gave, chose: ninguno lleva -ed.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el pasado del verbo entre paréntesis.
ejercicios.texto: Yesterday I {1} (wake) up late because I {2} (forget) to set the alarm. I {3} (make) a quick coffee, {4} (take) a cab and {5} (get) to the office at 9:15. My boss {6} (say) nothing, but she {7} (give) me a look. In the meeting, the client {8} (choose) option B, so we have a lot of work this week.
ejercicios.explica: Afirmativa del pasado simple = la segunda forma del verbo: wake → woke, forget → forgot, make → made, take → took, get → got, say → said, give → gave, choose → chose.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la forma correcta: pasado simple, o participio después de have.
ejercicios.texto: We have {1} (win) three pitches this year, but last week's was special. The team {2} (write) the proposal in four days. Andrés {3} (bring) the printed version and I {4} (send) the digital one. The client {5} (think) our idea was the best and {6} (tell) us the news on Friday. We {7} (spend) the whole evening celebrating, and I {8} (drink) a little too much.
ejercicios.explica: Después de have va el participio (have won). En la afirmativa del pasado va la segunda forma: wrote, brought, sent, thought, told, spent, drank (no drunk).

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la forma correcta: participio después de have, pasado simple en la historia.
ejercicios.texto: Have you ever {1} to New York? I have {2} there twice. The first time I {3} my passport at the hotel and {4} to the airport very late. The second time was better: I {5} the subway every day, {6} a Broadway show and {7} a lot of money on food. I have never {8} so much in one week.
ejercicios.explica: Have / has + participio (been, eaten); la historia concreta con tiempo definido va en pasado simple (forgot, got, took, saw, spent). 'Have you ever been to…?' usa been, no gone.

ejercicios.texto: Last weekend Camila and I drove to Villa de Leyva. We left Bogotá at 6 a.m. and got there at 9. We found a small hotel near the square and slept for an hour. Then we went sightseeing: we saw the main square, bought some bread and ate it in the park. In the afternoon we rode bikes to a small lake. Camila fell off her bike, but she didn't hurt herself. At night we met some friends from Medellín and drank wine until midnight. On Sunday I woke up late, forgot my sunglasses at the hotel and lost my keys for an hour. I found them in the car. We came back on Sunday afternoon, tired but happy. It was the best weekend I have had this year.

preguntas.q: How did they travel to Villa de Leyva?

opciones: She fell off her bike but didn't hurt herself

preguntas.q: Where did the writer find the keys?
«It was the best weekend I have had this year»: ¿qué forma es «had»?

ejercicios.explica: Veinte irregulares en pasado en una sola historia: drove, left, got, found, slept, went, saw, bought, ate, rode, fell, met, drank, woke, forgot, lost, came. Después de didn't va la base (didn't hurt).

ejercicios.texto: Hi team, here is a quick report of the week. On Monday we met the client and told her the plan for the launch. She chose option B and gave us two weeks. On Tuesday Andrés wrote the first draft and sent it to the media team. Laura brought the printed version to the meeting on Wednesday, and the client said she loved it. On Thursday we had a problem: the printer broke and we lost half a day. Mike found another printer and paid extra for fast delivery. On Friday we won the pitch for the bank! We have spent a little more than the budget, so I have spoken to finance. I haven't heard from them yet. Have a great weekend. Laura

preguntas.q: What was the problem on Thursday?
opciones: The printer broke and they lost half a day

preguntas.q: «I have spoken to finance»: ¿por qué «spoken» y no «spoke»?
opciones: Después de have va el participio

ejercicios.explica: Pasado simple para los hechos con día (met, told, chose, gave, wrote, sent, brought, said, broke, lost, found, paid, won) y have + participio para lo que sigue abierto (have spent, have spoken, haven't heard).

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta qué hiciste la semana pasada en el trabajo y en tu vida personal: usa al menos cinco verbos irregulares en pasado, una frase con have + participio y un marcador de tiempo (last week, on Monday, yesterday, … ago).

requisitos.texto: Usa al menos cinco pasados irregulares
Usa un marcador de pasado: yesterday, last week, on Monday, … ago

ejercicios.ejemplo: Last week was busy. On Monday I went to the gym at 6 and then I drove to the office. We met the client at 10 and she chose the second option. On Wednesday I wrote the proposal and sent it to the media team. On Friday we won the pitch, so we drank a few beers after work. At home, my son broke a glass and I lost my keys again. I have found them, but I haven't slept well all week.
ejercicios.explica: La historia va en pasado simple (segunda forma: went, drove, met, chose, wrote); lo que sigue conectado con el presente va con have + participio (have found, haven't slept).
